paragraphs: Pappos. Yuhasin writes (in the chronological section under R' Akiva): Pappos and Lulinos were given water in a colored glass vessel, but refused it and were killed for sanctification of the Name; Jerusalem Talmud, beginning of Shevi'it chapter 4, halakhah 2, and Jerusalem Talmud, Sanhedrin 3:5. In Ta'anit 18b, Turinus killed Lulinos and Pappos in Laodicea. Rashi explains that they were entirely righteous; Laodicea is Lod, and these are those called ‘the martyrs of Lod.’ Some say that they were killed because the king's daughter was found murdered and a decree of destruction was issued against Israel. They told him, ‘We killed her,’ to save Israel, and only these men were killed. The Arukh, entry הרג, writes that Shemaya and his brother were the martyrs of Lod, killed on 12 Adar, the Day of Trajan, at the end of Ta'anit chapter 2. It brings the aforementioned episode in Rashi, in which the king's daughter was found murdered; it does not explain as Rashi does that they were Pappos and Lulinos in Laodicea. ‘Laodicea’ supports Rashi. But in Kol Kitvei it appears that Laodicea is outside the Land and is not Lod; so too in Menahot 85b (as it also appears in Benjamin's Travels), as Rashi explained in Vayehi and in the Targum to Ve-Zot Ha-Berakhah, in Asher's blessing. (In Jerusalem Talmud, Sanhedrin, first chapter, halakhah 2: Lod is in Judea, and they do not intercalate the year there, because they are arrogant and have little Torah.) He likewise writes that there is a Lod outside the Land [Heilprin’s digital witness reads בארן], as in ‘The first hour is the eating time of the Ludim,’ who eat human flesh, and Resh Lakish sold himself to the Ludim (see there); likewise ‘Pul and Lud, drawers of the bow.’ But Lod, where R' Eliezer lived, was one day's journey from Jerusalem. According to the Gemara there are grounds for both views; also in the aforementioned Jerusalem Talmud and Tosafot, Kelal Gadol. This supports the author of the Arukh. In Bereshit Rabbah, chapter 64 (see R' Yehoshua ben Hananya): in the time of Turianus, Emperor Hadrian's father [as the source describes him], Lulinos and Pappos set up trapezin (meaning tables) and provided for those coming up from exile. Here ends Yuhasin. See Midrash Kohelet, on ‘Whatever your hand finds to do’: R' Aha longed to see R' Alexandri's face (in a dream, since he was already dead). They showed him two things in a dream: ‘The martyrs of Lod’ (Mattenot Kehunah explains: Pappos and Lulinos, as above; Rashi likewise explains in Ellu Overin 50a and the first chapter of Bava Batra, whereas the Arukh explains: Shemaya and his brother)—‘none is within their enclosure’; ‘Blessed is He who removed the disgrace of Lulinos and Pappos.’ (Mattenot Kehunah writes: see the passage ‘I said in my heart’: when they were killed by Turkhinus in Laodicea, etc., they had not managed to move from there before envoys came from Rome and crushed his brain with clubs. The reading is ‘They showed him three things.’ End quotation.) ‘And happy is he who comes here with his learning in his hand.’ In Sifra [כ in source], Emor: ‘When Turianus seized.’ At the end of Semahot chapter 8: ‘[When] Tragoanus [killed] Pappos and Lulinos in Laodicea’.
